topic.title: Software-Engineering Agents and Workflow Evaluation
topic.overview: Software agents must inspect repositories, modify code, run tools, and respond to execution results. This topic studies environments and evaluations that capture those interactions, extending beyond isolated code generation. It also includes statistical debugging and operational analysis, where learning helps identify the causes or locations of software problems.
topic.whyItMatters: Passing a familiar benchmark can overstate capability if tasks are contaminated or cover only a narrow workflow. Realistic evaluation requires executable environments, diverse languages and task types, and evidence that changes solve the intended problem. Automated judges introduce their own reliability questions.
topic.evolution: A 2010 method mines console logs using program analysis and learned event features. Recent work turns repositories into agent environments and evaluates software optimization. SWE-rebench in 2025 continuously extracts interactive tasks to support fresher evaluation; SWE-Compass in 2026 broadens coverage across task types, scenarios, and programming languages.
openQuestions: How can automated evaluations verify intended behavior beyond passing existing tests?
Which benchmarks measure sustained repository work without becoming rapidly contaminated?

papers.tldr: SWE-ABS strengthens software-repair tests and rejects nearly one fifth of previously passing patches, substantially changing benchmark scores and rankings.

papers.title: SWE-Bench Pro: Can AI Agents Solve Long-Horizon Software Engineering Tasks?
papers.tldr: SWE-Bench Pro tests realistic repository-scale engineering and reveals substantial capability gaps on complex, multi-file tasks.

papers.title: SWE-Compass: Towards Unified Evaluation of Agentic Coding Abilities for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: SWE-Compass evaluates coding agents on 2,000 real pull-request tasks spanning eight task types, eight scenarios, and ten languages.

papers.title: SWE-fficiency: Can Language Models Optimize Real-World Repositories on Real Workloads?
papers.tldr: SWE-fficiency tests real repository optimization and finds that leading agents achieve less than 0.23 times expert speedup on average.

papers.title: SWE-Milestone: Evaluating AI Agents on Continuous Software Evolution
papers.tldr: SWE-Milestone evaluates connected software-development sequences and finds a sharp performance drop when agents must maintain a system over time.

papers.title: SWE-MiniSandbox: Container-Free Reinforcement Learning for Building Software Engineering Agents
papers.tldr: SWE-MiniSandbox uses kernel-backed isolated workspaces to cut training-environment overhead while maintaining comparable agent performance.

papers.title: SWE-Perf: Can Language Models Optimize Code Performance on Real-World Repositories?
papers.tldr: SWE-Perf benchmarks repository-level code optimization and finds a substantial gap between language-model methods and expert performance improvements.

papers.title: SWE-rebench V2: Language-Agnostic SWE Task Collection at Scale
papers.tldr: SWE-rebench V2 automates collection of executable software-engineering tasks across languages, releasing large datasets and reproducible training infrastructure.

papers.title: TestExplora: Benchmarking LLMs for Proactive Bug Discovery via Repository-Level Test Generation
papers.tldr: TestExplora measures bug discovery without defect clues and finds that proactive repository testing remains difficult, with gains from agentic exploration.

papers.title: ThunderAgent: A Fast, Simple, and Program-Aware Agentic Inference System
papers.tldr: ThunderAgent coordinates model and tool resources across complete agent programs, improving evaluated throughput and disk-memory efficiency.

papers.title: Toward Training Superintelligent Software Agents through Self-Play SWE-RL
papers.tldr: Self-play SWE-RL trains an agent to create and repair repository bugs without human-labeled issues, producing gains on two software-repair benchmarks.

papers.title: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
papers.tldr: Twelve reliability metrics reveal that recent agent capability gains have brought only small reliability improvements across the evaluated models and benchmarks.

papers.title: Training Language Model Agents to Find Vulnerabilities with CTF-Dojo
papers.tldr: CTF-Dojo provides reproducible executable security challenges whose verified training trajectories improve agent performance across three CTF benchmarks.

papers.title: Tvcache: A Tool-Value Cache for Post-Training LLM Agents
papers.tldr: TVCACHE reuses tool outputs only for matching interaction histories, reducing tool latency without degrading reward accumulation in the evaluated workloads.

papers.title: UltraHorizon: Benchmarking Agent Capabilities in Ultra Long-Horizon Scenarios
papers.tldr: UltraHorizon exposes persistent weaknesses in agents’ sustained exploration, planning, and memory use across very long discovery tasks.

papers.title: VenusBench-Mobile: A Challenging and User-Centric Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents with Capability Diagnostics
papers.tldr: VenusBench-Mobile tests mobile agents on user-centered tasks and exposes major perception, memory, and environmental-robustness failures.

papers.title: VeRO: A Harness for Agents to Optimize Agents
papers.tldr: VeRO provides versioning, controlled evaluation, execution traces, and a benchmark for studying how coding agents improve other agents.

papers.title: Vision2Web: A Hierarchical Benchmark for Visual Website Development with Agent Verification
papers.tldr: Vision2Web evaluates website-building agents from static interfaces through full-stack workflows and reveals substantial capability gaps.

papers.title: When Replanning Becomes the Bottleneck: Budgeted Replanning for Embodied Agents
papers.tldr: BRACE budgets each replanning call and prunes context to reduce deadline violations while supporting embodied-agent task success.
